hard_failures.nearest_hf: HF-06 (assumption_smuggling) - nearest code; the taxonomy has no exact 'formal-expansion != declared predicate' code. Also violates A0 G-FORM criterion 2 ('exact quantifier prefix').
hard_failures.label: B
hard_failures.finding: Operative quantifier expansion contradicts the canonical visibility predicate (whole curve vs tail). quantifiers.formal (lines 47-55, decisive clause at 54-55: 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M') and domain D5 (lines 79-81: q such that 'gamma([0,T)) is contained in ... J^-(q)') use whole-curve single-q non-containment, and quantifiers.ordered (56-62) binds no t0. visibility.definition (line 220) defines visibility with the tail ('exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q)') and visibility.negation_conclusion (line 222) is the matching tail negation ('for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail ... is NOT contained'). Since whole-curve containment A(q) implies tail containment B(q,t0) and not conversely, 'not exists q A(q)' is STRICTLY WEAKER than 'not exists q exists t0 B(q,t0)'. quantifiers.negation (84-88) negates the tail predicate ('some ... geodesic ... is visible from I+'), so the formal block and its declared negation are not complements of each other. The R1-F02 tail correction was propagated to the visibility block (R1 tags at 220/222, note at 227) but not into quantifiers.formal/ordered/D5; the earlier whole-curve reading survives in the operative statement and in statement_formal (line 251) only as the undefined symbol AF_{I+}. The class is therefore stated weaker than its own definition, which the artifact's forbidden_weakenings (262-266, 'using a weaker visibility notion or a different definition of singular point') prohibits.

hard_failures.falsifier: Define quantifiers.formal with a t0 binder and the tail predicate, redefine D5 as the tail set, and show formal == visibility.negation_conclusion. Claiming the readings equivalent requires exhibiting the converse implication B=>A, which is false in general.

hard_failures.nearest_hf: HF-06-adjacent / A0 G-FORM criterion 2 ('exact quantifier prefix, no or') and criterion 3 ('data space named with topology + regularity + decay + constraint + end structure')
hard_failures.label: B
hard_failures.finding: D0 is not well-typed for its binder: a disjunction of two regularity classes under one pair-indexed symbol. D0 (63-66) is 'admissible regularity pairs: Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), OR the smooth-with-decay default', while ordered[0] (line 57) binds '(s,delta)', and the ambient space/generic set are pair-indexed (X^{s,delta}_vac and G_{s,delta} at 49 and 251; data_class.regularity_class at 114-120). No symbol for the smooth branch (e.g. X^smooth_vac / G_smooth) is defined anywhere in the document. The class statement is therefore a disjunction of two formal statements, with the smooth branch not expressible in the declared notation; two competent readers can differ on what the smooth branch quantifies over, triggering schema_falsifiers[0] (imprecise schema). A0 G-FORM explicitly forbids 'or' in the exact quantifier prefix, and the artifact itself declares its values fixed (63-66).
hard_failures.falsifier: Index the class by a regularity-specification set R with a symbol X^r_vac for each r in R (or emit two separate class statements), so that the binder, the ambient space and the generic set all have the same type and no 'or' remains.

'revised_at' occurs 7 times (lines 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 23) and 'revised_at_unused' twice (26, 28); YAML 1.2 forbids duplicate mapping keys, and spec-compliant strict parsers reject the file, while PyYAML silently keeps the last occurrence.
